# Sparse diagonal stroke continuation

## When to use
Use when an ARC grid has a mostly uniform background and compact sparse motifs that may encode diagonal lines extended to grid boundaries. This is a class-level hypothesis workflow, not an ID-specific answer recipe.

## Workflow
1. Record all non-background coordinates and group by color. Separate same-color aligned pairs/segments from isolated cells and from mixed-color diagonal chains.
2. For each plausible same-color segment, test both diagonal orientations (down-right/up-left and down-left/up-right). Identify segment endpoints and compute exact ray cells to boundaries without altering the seed.

# task-a1ff7ccc: connect aligned diamond motifs

## Confirmed instance rule
Each motif is a four-cell diamond/cross with no center: for center `(r,c)`, color-2 cells at `(r-1,c)`, `(r,c-1)`, `(r,c+1)`, `(r+1,c)`. Find motif centers from the four surrounding color-2 cells (center cell itself is background/0).

Connect motif pairs that share a row or column by drawing color 1 in the cells strictly between their facing horizontal or vertical tips. Preserve all original 2s and all other cells. For horizontal aligned centers `(r,c1),(r,c2)`, fill row `r` from `min(c1,c2)+2` through `max(c1,c2)-2` inclusive (the tips at `c+1`/`c-1` remain 2). For vertical aligned centers `(r1,c),(r2,c)`, analogously fill column `c` strictly between the tips: rows `min(r1,r2)+2` through `max(r1,r2)-2` inclusive. Demonstrated with centers separated by 7 horizontally (four 1s) and 4 vertically (one 1). Only bridge aligned pairs; do not connect diagonal centers.

## Accepted test evidence
Test contained centers `(2,2),(4,7),(6,2),(6,10)` in zero-based coordinates. Correct output adds 1 at `(4,2)` bridging the vertical pair `(2,2)-(6,2)`, and at `(6,4..8)` bridging horizontal pair `(6,2)-(6,10)`. All else unchanged. Demo had centers `(1,3),(1,10),(5,10)`, and added 1 at `(1,5..8)` and `(3,10)`.

## Pitfalls / validation
- Keep grid dimensions exactly unchanged and every row exactly the input width; a malformed row count/length was rejected as “not a valid ARC grid.”
- The first geometrically intended response contained a row-length error; a corrected, width-15 output still failed because it omitted a bridge between the vertically aligned lower/upper diamonds. A later output including both vertical and horizontal bridges was accepted.
- Detect pairs based on center alignment, not proximity alone. Do not alter motif cells."
}
